_comment: Environment + provider defaults used by authoring agents and page templates.
_templateComment: Notes-page template the authors copy (D-0031): the promoted W1D2 page. args_for.py passes it as args.template; when the file is missing it falls back to harness/templates/day.exemplar.html, which stays the structure gold standard for the tests.

audience._comment: Learner persona (D-0023, superseded by D-0048). Reaches every author/critic prompt as 'Audience'. Change via a decision entry.
audience.summary: Recent computer-science graduates (University of Toronto cohort) with no industry experience. Backgrounds vary and what each trainee retained is unknown.
assumeKnown: general programming ideas from any language: a variable, a branch, a loop, a function
assumeNotKnown: Python: its syntax, types, idioms and standard library
Git and GitHub, including clone, add, commit and push
the terminal: shells, paths, running a program from a prompt
CS theory: compilers vs interpreters, data structures, OOP
audience.rule: Never write that the reader already knows something, met it in coursework or remembers it. Teach each idea on its home day; an idea used before its home day gets a one-line explanation where it is used.
emphasise: how professional teams actually work: SDLC, Scrum, code review, written communication
Python from first principles: the syntax first, then the idioms, conventions and pitfalls a team expects
Git from first principles, then the team workflow: branches, merges, conflicts, remotes, commit hygiene
theory taught briefly and concretely, then practice

learnerRepo._comment: Learner repo convention (D-0051, supersedes D-0037): one PUBLIC repository per trainee inside the cohort organisation, created in the W1D2 Git exercise and kept for the whole course. Reaches every exercise and runbook author/critic prompt through args_for.py and day-fanout.js (learnerCtx). The trainer's live demo repository is demoRepo below, a different repository. Change via a decision entry.
learnerRepo.name: FirstnameLastname
learnerRepo.nameRule: the trainee's first and last name as on the class roster, run together in PascalCase, ASCII letters and digits; a hyphen or underscore between the names is tolerated; a clash gets a trailing digit

layout.root: hello.py, .gitignore and README.md from the W1D2 Git exercise stay at the top level
layout.exercises: <week-dir>/<day-slug>/, the same relative path the exercise has under exercises/ in the training repo
layout.hackathon: <week-dir>/hackathon/ for the week's hackathon deliverable, due on the week's last teaching day unless the trainer says otherwise
layout.codeAlong: optional: code-along/<week-dir>/<day-slug>/ for the trainee's own copy of what was typed in class; never marked

learnerRepo.handIn: commit and push to main; the trainer reads the day's folder in the trainee's repository

demoRepo._comment: The trainer's live demo repository (D-0050): a PUBLIC GitHub repo separate from this one, cloned at localDir (gitignored, like trainer/). Loose days (demoFormat loose) are typed under layout.loose; thread code from week 3 lives under threads.<id>.repoDir. harness/close_day.py reads it to close a day. Replaces the team-repo wording of D-0033 and D-0037. Change via a decision entry.
demoRepo.name: demos

layout.loose: <week-dir>/<day-slug>/ (the day's rel, the same path as everywhere else); any filenames
layout.thread: <threads.<id>.repoDir>/ at the top level, e.g. ticket-desk/ticket_desk.py, one commit per rung

llm.rule: Model ids are resolved in the research brief from current docs, never from memory.

models._comment: Per-stage model and effort for harness/workflows/day-fanout.js, week-plan.js and practice-tasks.js (D-0026, D-0032, D-0040, D-0047). model: sonnet | haiku | opus; effort: low | medium | high | xhigh | max. Every stage is pinned: no stage inherits the session model (D-0040), and tests/test_notes_mode.py fails a null. A repass numbered >= escalateOn uses escalate instead of the stage tier, so a cheap first pass that fails its critic is retried on the strong tier. notes-critic judges the notes page; notes-verify-light runs harness/notes_check.py (links, stamps, citations) on every day; notes-verify-full adds WebFetch claim currency on full-gate and currency-flagged days. practice-suitability proposes practice tasks for an authored page and practice builds the approved ones (D-0047); their critic, verify and record agents use critic, verify and wire.

threads._comment: Demo threads (D-0033, D-0034, D-0050): one demo codebase per project block that grows rung by rung across days and weeks. repoDir and file name where the thread lives inside demoRepo (one commit per rung, the rung-diff close reads it from week 3). args_for.py --plan passes the threads whose week range covers the week; the week-plan author may not invent a thread. Add P1/P2 threads via a decision entry before their first week is planned.

p0-ticket-desk.domain: A support-ticket desk for a small software team: tickets with a title, priority, status and history, filed by customers and triaged by agents. Week 1 keeps tickets in Python variables, lists, dicts and classes; week 2 splits the desk into modules with logging, JSON files, regex on ticket text and pytest; week 3 moves tickets, customers and agents into MySQL tables with joins and transactions on assignment; week 4 loads ticket events into a BigQuery star schema through an ETL job; week 5 sends tickets to an LLM for triage, summaries and draft replies.

tracker._comment: Alarm thresholds for tracker.html (D-0035), in calendar days. Readiness follows the previous-Friday rule: a day that is not live turns amber dayAmberDaysBeforeWeek days before its week's Monday (the Wednesday before) and red dayRedDaysBeforeWeek days before (the Friday before). The browser applies these to today's date; harness/build_tracker.py only embeds them.

trainerRepo.note: Separate private git repo cloned at ./trainer and gitignored by this repo.
